text: Agents that optimize your code like an algorithm engineer: a falsifiable hypothesis before every experiment, correctness checked after every change, one reviewable patch per accepted change, and a PDF report of the whole session. A skill for Claude Code and Codex, from the Algorithm Engineering Group at Heidelberg University. Every kept change was checked against the original output. Algorithm Engineering is a cycle of design, analysis, implementation and experiment, driven by falsifiable hypotheses. AAE hands this cycle to an autonomous agent. During setup you agree with the agent on the benchmark, the metric, the correctness assertions and the budget; then it runs on its own. A falsifiable hypothesis: "changing X will improve the metric by roughly Z, because ..." Predict direction and size of the effect before measuring, from profiling and analysis. A minimal change, committed to Git, with the correctness assertions checked. Run the benchmark; keep the change only if it is better and still correct, otherwise revert. From the report of the KaHIP kaffpa session: 122 experiments, 69 hypotheses, 41 patches, 3.9x faster in total. In Claude Code: /plugin install aae --marketplace CHSZLab/AgenticAlgorithmEngineering /aae:aae make the solver in src/ faster on the graphs in data/ In Codex, install the skill with scripts/install_codex_skill.py and call it with $aae ; any other agent can follow AAE.md . To try it first, run the 10-minute quick-start example : a slow but correct shortest-path program with a benchmark and a correctness check. Sessions share what they learned: the knowledge base collects optimization techniques and experiment results, and agents read it before they start. Contributions from your own sessions are welcome. David A. Bader, Adil Chhabra, Ernestine Großmann, Monika Henzinger, Alexander Noe, and Christian Schulz. Agentic Algorithm Engineering: Improving Shared-Memory Exact Minimum Cuts. In 13th DIMACS Implementation Challenge Workshop: Network Flows 2.0, OASIcs, 2027. To appear.
